<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via insertManyData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via insertManyData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via insertManyData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 70 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c139b7f3c17d3452fff2cbfd8eefdd36ccb08109` — the merge of head `886ad2c43ee3a561d9f81bc41f65de09f8a3a8b6` into base `2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c139b7f3c17d3452fff2cbfd8eefdd36ccb08109 && git checkout c139b7f3c17d3452fff2cbfd8eefdd36ccb08109
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4 886ad2c43ee3a561d9f81bc41f65de09f8a3a8b6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4 && git merge --no-ff 886ad2c43ee3a561d9f81bc41f65de09f8a3a8b6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `886ad2c43ee3a561d9f81bc41f65de09f8a3a8b6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20922 (its body and all five comments, 5919693532 through 5924083608), PR #21041 (its body, its eight-file list, and the net diff of the branch head against merge-base `2f2fa11d7`), and the 40 check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-01T03:33Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run; `git fetch`, `git diff`, `git show` and `git grep` over the shared checkout were the only local acts.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface, as the two packages' `.d.ts` publish it:
1. `@objectstack/objectql` — `InsertManyRowOutcome` (exported at `index.ts:279`; the element of `ObjectQL.insertMany`'s declared answer): its `ok: true` arm gains `droppedFields?: DroppedFieldsEvent[]`. An additive optional key on a published type — a widening. **Right.**
2. `@objectstack/objectql` — `ObjectQL.validate`: declared answer unchanged (`ValidateDataResponse` from spec, whose `results[].droppedFields` #20921 declared). The behaviour now fills that key on each accepted row. No `.d.ts` movement; a pre-declared key produced. **Right.**
3. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.insertManyData`: the declared `outcomes` element gains `droppedFields?: DroppedFieldsEvent[]`; the top-level `droppedFields` union slot and the union docblock above the signature are untouched. An additive widening. **Right.**
4. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — `validateData`: signature and body untouched (a TSDoc note only); it returns `engine.validate`'s answer whole, so the per-row key rides through. No listener is forwarded (the card title's mechanism): `ValidateDataResponse` has no batch-level slot, and triage's unlock 5919741392 had already said forwarding alone cannot fill a per-row key. What the scope asks for — the answer carries the drops in #20921's declared key — is met. **Right.**
5. `@objectstack/spec` — `protocol.zod.ts` (hunk at `:2119`) and `export.zod.ts` (hunk at `:327`): every changed line is a ` *` TSDoc line. No non-comment line moved; no schema, `.describe()` or inferred type moved; no generated artifact and no changeset entry is owed. **Right.**
   - The new `ValidateDataResponseSchema` prose states only what this head does. Read against `validate` at the head: `stripComputedWriteFields` runs in every context (before the `isSystem` gate); under `!isSystem` the runtime-owned and static-`readonly` strips run in `insert` mode and `stripReadonlyFields` in `update` mode; each records per row (`computedStrip.droppedPerRow`, `readonlyDroppedPerRow`); the key is set only on the `valid: true` return; `validateData` relays it; `readonlyWhen` and the primary-key strip are not run on an `update`-mode preview (the engine's own comment at the strips says the same). One omission, not a falsehood: the runtime-owned strip is also `preserveAudit`-exempt, which the sentence folds under "`isSystem`-gated".
   - The new `ImportRowResultSchema` prose: `git grep` over `packages/rest/src/import-*.test.ts` at the head finds `warnings` read only off synchronous-route responses (`import-dryrun-parity.test.ts:204`; `import-integration.test.ts:824`, a direct `route.handler` call with no job poll). "No test reads it off the async job's results" holds.
   - The `droppedFields` bullet left standing in `export.zod.ts` ("until both do, no server sets the key") stays true: the REST route does not copy the report yet.

Accept set: unchanged everywhere. Nothing is newly refused or admitted. `strictReadonlyWrites` still refuses the whole batch before any outcome is built (the `insertDrops` branch is the same, now fed by the builder); the declared-field door and the computed strip's `refused` skip are as they were. **Right.**

Batch-level union: `validate`'s and `insert`'s `onFieldsDropped` events are built by the new `droppedFieldEvents(object, computed, readonly)` from the same `computedStrip.dropped` / `readonlyDropped` / `insertDropped` arrays — one event per reason, `computed` then `readonly`, naming no row. Content identical to the base; the one observable difference is that an event now carries a copy of the array rather than the engine's own, which no contract exposes. `insert(object, rows[])` outside partial mode still returns the records. **Right.**

Per-row attribution, judged at the code: recorded at the strips (`droppedPerRow` inside `stripComputedWriteFields`; `recordTaken` in `validate`; `recordInsertTaken` in `insert`), never derived from the union — the `hookWrittenKeys` case (one row's `beforeInsert` keeps the key, its sibling loses it) is pinned, and it is the case a reconstruction gets wrong. Index alignment holds: in `validate`, `submittedRows` → `computedStrip.rows` → `rows` (one map, same length and order) → `results` mapped over `rows` by index; in `insert` partial mode, `computedStrip` runs over `opCtx.data` with `undeclaredPerRow`, `rows` is `rowHookContexts` in input order, and the outcome map reads index `i` of both per-row arrays. A refused or failed row gets `[]` at the strips and `ok: false` at the outcome, so it carries none. **Right.**

Scope item 3 (no second strip, no second reason vocabulary): one builder, one `reason` set (`computed`, `readonly`), the same `DroppedFieldsEvent` element from `@objectstack/spec/data`. **Right.**

Pins the card names: a formula column (`computed`) and a `readonly` column (`readonly`) through dry run and commit, the clean-row control, and the unchanged union are pinned in the new `engine-per-row-dropped-fields.test.ts`, at the engine and through the real protocol, beside a refused row and a failed outcome carrying none, `isSystem`, `update` mode, the hook-exempted row, and the non-partial `insert`. The `engine-autonumber-runtime-owned.test.ts` case that pinned "names no row" now pins the row's own outcome beside the unchanged union; `protocol.dropped-fields.bulk.test.ts` pins pass-through with nothing derived at the seam. **Right.**

Docs named by the drift comment (5924017625). `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`: every sentence read stays true — the listener still fires once per strip pass with the union, `DroppedFieldsEvent` is unchanged, and the Callout's "`insertManyData` ... surface this seam's `onFieldsDropped` as their response `droppedFields`" still describes the top-level union; the page says nothing about per-row attribution, so the new channel contradicts nothing (a gap the REST carrier can fill, not a falsehood). `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`: names `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` only for `getOverlayRepo()` and layered metadata, which this diff does not touch. No sentence on either page is made false.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/20922-per-row-dropped-fields.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`. Each package's `.d.ts` gains an optional key on a published answer (items 1 and 3 above): an additive widening, nothing removed, renamed or refused, so `minor` is the level the WHICH LEVEL rule gives. `@objectstack/spec` carries no entry and none is owed: its diff is TSDoc only and publishes no surface change. The body describes what the diff does, the unchanged union and the `update`-mode limit included. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — PR body line 2, as the seat answer 5924083608 regraded the claim's `no`. A consumer typed by either package can read a key it could not before, so `yes` is the truthful value; `(widening)` is the matching arm of the closed pair (`clause2-line.mjs` lists `yes (widening)` as a well-formed spelling); `yes` takes at least `minor`, which both entries are. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker are owed: nothing narrows. **Right.**
- Gate read: `Check Changeset` (the `changeset-check` job, which runs `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` against the PR body's `Clause-②` line and re-runs on `edited`) succeeded twice on this head; the second run (36810354039) started after the PR body's last edit, so the `yes (widening)` line, not the claim's `no`, is the one it passed. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Lint & Repo Gates` succeeded. The declaration, the changeset and its gates read consistently. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions (report 5924041038):
- Q1, an `update`-mode preview runs no `readonlyWhen` / primary-key strip — the seat answered **A** (keep the named limit). Judged: answered, and right for this card. The limit pre-dates this PR (the engine's own comment at the strips), the key's `.describe()` already says absence proves nothing, and this head writes the limit into the `ValidateDataResponseSchema` TSDoc and the changeset; the commit still reports the drop on its own channel. Option B is a preview-contract change with no measured pull; C discards exact information. Not escalated.
- Q2, the `Clause-②` line — the seat answered **B** and edited the body to `yes (widening)`. Judged right in ② above. Not escalated.

Deviations (five):
- No listener forwarded from `validateData` — judged right in ① item 4; the card's pins are met by the engine's own answer.
- `origin/main` merged (the head is a merge of `2f2fa11d7`) before the final gate derivation — the net diff against the merge-base is the eight files above and nothing else. No flag.
- The first `vitest` launch was relaunched with its flag read correctly, and no measurement came from the first. Hygiene; no flag.
- Unit and package tests ran at `24ca898f8` / `99a7547af`, the gate union at the head — the merge brought in no file this PR touches; the head's own test verdict is CI's (below). No flag.
- The `protocol.zod.ts` sentence became two — both inside the one docblock the card named. No flag.

Dev-declared NOT MEASURED, answered by the head's check-runs: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is hosted by `Build Core` — success; `check:type-check-debt` by `Type Check · debt ledger` — success. The `packages/runtime` integration tier is CI's `Test Core` — still in progress (below).

Out-of-scope findings (two, carried to the PR that lands #20701's REST item 1): the half-stale `ImportRowResultSchema` bullet is still true, and `ImportProtocolLike.insertManyData` in `packages/rest/src/import-runner.ts` types its outcomes without the optional key, which the real protocol still satisfies. Carried, not filed — rightly.

Check-runs on the head (40, read at the time stamped above): 26 success; 5 skipped (`Auto Label`, `Build Docs`, `Check PR Size`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` — path-skipped, not verdicts against this diff); and 9 still `in_progress`, which are NOT verdicts and are named as such: `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (the aggregate; its three shards succeeded), and `Type Check · workspace`. The landing rule needs every check green; this record does not wait for them.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Ujdtvqs7ree7WyQmEDwEnG`

**VERDICT: PASS**
